newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bonds hold, depos,swaps softer in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Greek bonds hold, depos,swaps softer in late trade.

text.p: Greek bonds were holding, depos and forex forwards were trading lower and ecu/drachma was weaker after local investors sold ecus for drachmas in late Wednesday trade, dealers said.
"Depos and swaps are trading lower late on Wednesday," a state bank dealer said.
The Bank of Greece drained 200 billion drachmas of 14-day funds at 11.90 percent in Wednesday's money tender. The fixed rate tender was oversubscribed.
A 14-day depo pact for 200 billion drachmas expires today, so liquidity is virtually unchanged.
"The market was indifferent to the results of the auction as there was no change in liquidity," the dealer said.
The bond market was very quiet in late dealings, a foreign bank bond dealer said.

"Ever since news of an easing CPI March inflation were released, it looks as if funds shifted from the bond market to the stock exchange. Bonds' profit margins and spreads have become smaller," the dealer said.
Overall, bonds seem to be on a slight uptrend because of the money market's recent downward movement, the dealer added.
The ecu/drachma rate was lower late on Wednesday after some sales of ecus for drachmas by local investors, a foreign bank forex dealer said.
"Ecu/drachma is trading at 307.20, lower than it opened in the morning. It fell after fixing when some Greek investors started selling ecus for drachmas," the dealer said.
The mark was quoted at 157.35/45 from Wednesday's 157.465 fix, the dollar at 270.34/44 drachmas from 270.190 and the ecu at 307.41/51 from 307.490 drachmas.
